gates.reason: Parses uploaded text into bounded structures without filesystem writes, command execution, HTML injection, network egress, or credential disclosure.
Re-derived percentages, latency percentiles, age calculations, churn scores, timestamps, and backup diffs; inputs are type-checked and calculations are reproducible from uploaded fields.
Collection is linear over uploaded files; per-artifact scans and sorting are bounded by the admitted upload dataset and introduce no nested per-request recomputation.
Tests explicitly verify filtered credentials and metadata-only secret bodies never cross the upload result boundary.
Tests cover usable-file accounting, session identity, parse-only isolation, and explicit project attribution.
Test code is not a production hot path.
The upload orchestrator performs no filesystem writes or egress and posts parsed structures rather than raw transcript text; archive filtering is delegated to the unzip boundary.
History, session, transcript, memory, workflow, and artifact results retain their source-derived identifiers and deterministic parse flow.
All decoded loose and archive entries accumulate in one LoadedFile array and remain live through every parse pass, so batching does not cap peak ingest memory.
The parser coordinator dynamically imports fixed local modules and neither executes uploaded commands nor performs filesystem/network operations.
Each emitted result is produced directly by a named parser pass; null filtering and flattening preserve the pass outputs without fabricating claims.
Passes are intentionally worker-side, dynamic imports avoid eager entry-bundle weight, and the main-thread fallback uses chunked yielding.
Uses a fixed module-worker URL, passes Blob handles through structured clone, and exposes no raw-data or script-injection sink.
Worker completion, failure fallback, status dispatch, and parsed-result dispatch preserve the pipeline envelope.
Worker execution is preferred, the fallback module is dynamically loaded, and fallback parsing enables event-loop yielding.
The worker accepts structured upload inputs and posts parsed messages; it has no filesystem, command, DOM, or independent network sink.
It forwards the dataset builder's messages and summary without transformation and reports failures explicitly.
CPU-heavy inflation and parsing are kept off the UI thread and the worker is a minimal entry surface.
Scheduler unit tests do not handle authentication, secrets, filesystems, web rendering, commands, or network boundaries.
Tests verify ordering, bounded batching, immediate flushing, cancellation, and pending-count behavior.
Test harness code is not a production hot path.
The in-memory callback scheduler has no security-sensitive boundary or sink.
Queue order is preserved across batch flushes, flushNow, and cancellation without duplication.
Default batches are capped, idle callbacks have a timeout fallback, and only one scheduled flush is outstanding.
The test suite explicitly requires an MCP-only access token to be accepted, preserving unsafe credential selection.
Tests cover finite header parsing, reset/status handling, availability reasons, overage parsing, and representative claims.
Pure unit tests are not a production hot path.
findAccessToken falls back to the first arbitrary accessToken, allowing an MCP OAuth secret from ~/.claude credentials to be selected for Anthropic egress.
Usage and reset values are parsed with finite-number checks, and payload availability is derived deterministically from response headers and status.
Credential traversal and header assembly are linear, small, server-side operations with no repeated network work in this module.
This types-only module performs no authentication, egress, rendering, filesystem, or command operation.
It declares response shapes and performs no parsing, arithmetic, or recommendation calculation.
Types are erased at runtime and add no bundle execution cost.
Tests verify the SPA/server availability guard and ensure obsolete or disabled-source responses cannot overwrite current client state.
Tests exercise scope changes, dataset generations, expiry boundaries, clock rollback, retries, and stale-response rejection.
Test code is not a production render hot path.
The SPA remains viewer-only, fetches through the API-client boundary, aborts obsolete requests, and exposes no HTML or script sink.
Recommendations are shown only for ready responses; scope changes and expired snapshots fail closed, including after clock rollback.
Requests are scope-keyed and aborted on replacement; callbacks and effects are memoized and no detector catalog enters the SPA path.
Stored values are restricted to good/bad tags and returned as data; the hook contains no HTML rendering or external egress sink.
Corrupt storage fails to an empty map, values are validated, and same-tab plus cross-tab changes resynchronize state.
Storage is read only on initialization or change events, writes avoid no-op updates, and listeners are cleaned up.

findings.title: Upload batching does not bound peak decoded-text memory
findings.what: Every loose-file body is decoded and appended to the long-lived loaded array; every inflated archive entry is then appended as well. The complete decoded corpus remains reachable while session aggregation and all parser passes run. The file itself documents a representative 634 MB admitted-text upload at lines 7-8, so the claimed batching at line 142 only limits concurrent reads, not peak memory, and can cause worker termination or main-thread fallback memory pressure.
findings.fix: Process admitted files incrementally or partition metadata, history, auxiliary artifacts, and sessions so decoded bodies are released after their consuming passes; enforce an admitted decoded-byte budget before retaining additional text.
findings.acceptance: Add an ingest memory-budget probe using a multi-file corpus larger than the configured budget and verify the pipeline either streams/releases completed bodies or rejects before retained decoded text exceeds that budget, while producing identical parsed results for an in-budget corpus.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed loaded is initialized once at line 125, all batch results and archive entries are appended at lines 168 and 185, and the retained collection is still consumed at line 220 and later; no deletion, clearing, streaming, or decoded-byte cap exists in this file.

findings.title: MCP OAuth credentials can be sent to Anthropic as subscription credentials
findings.what: If ~/.claude/.credentials.json contains access tokens but none has the sk-ant-oat prefix or a Claude-named parent, findAccessToken returns the first arbitrary token. The test explicitly requires an MCP-only credential to be returned. The directly related server caller uses that return value as the OAuth credential for an Anthropic /messages request, so an MCP secret can leave ~/.claude in violation of the subscription-credential egress rule.
findings.fix: Fail closed unless the candidate is positively identified as the Claude subscription OAuth credential, preferably by the sk-ant-oat prefix or a narrowly validated Claude credential schema; remove the arbitrary first-token fallback and change the MCP-only test to expect null.
findings.acceptance: Given credentials containing only mcpOAuth accessToken values, findAccessToken returns null and no Anthropic call is made; valid sk-ant-oat and explicitly supported Claude subscription credential shapes still resolve, including when MCP tokens appear first.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read lines 45-52 and the MCP-only assertion at test lines 46-48, then inspected only the direct baseline caller, which reads ~/.claude/.credentials.json and passes the selected token to the Anthropic /messages egress chokepoint. The candidate is therefore reproducible and not merely a naming concern.
